_what_this_is: The goals the loop is working TOWARD, each with a machine-readable done-condition. ⛔ THIS IS NOT THE LEDGER. The ledger holds ITEMS — units of work a cycle can take; this holds OBJECTIVES, which no single cycle completes and which outlive the cycle that advances them. An item is done when its work is done; a goal is done when a condition computed from committed artifacts says so.
_why_this_exists:
⛔⛔ THE ONE REAL GOAL IN PLAY WAS PROSE IN A DIFFERENT FILE'S SCOPE NOTE, AND NOTHING READ IT. trimcrae set 'get ASO v2 submission ready' on 2026-08-30 and it lived inside `autonomy-state.json`'s `budget_hold.authorised_exceptions` — a field about SPENDING — where it authorised a budget exception and tracked nothing. Meanwhile `publish_bar` computes seven clauses from committed artifacts, `health.py` grades twelve conditions and `continuity.py` refuses to go quiet while ready work exists. The goal that justified spending against a budget hold was the least instrumented object in the system.
⚠ MEASURED 2026-09-01 (CYC-0090), and it is why this file exists rather than being a good idea: a full session of real work — a published Zenodo archive, two hardening rounds, four process defects found and fixed — moved `publish_bar` from 4/7 to 4/7. Every individual step was warranted. Nothing measured the distance to the objective, so nothing could say the distance had not closed. trimcrae asked for it directly: 'For now, the loop should just track the goal of the ASO paper.'
_how_to_read_it: `python3 research/autonomy/goal_progress.py --check`. It computes each goal's done-condition live and prints the distance. ⛔ IT NEVER READS A STORED VERDICT: `readings` below is a HISTORY for spotting a goal that is not moving, and a reader who trusts it instead of recomputing has the staleness problem this file was built to end (CLAUDE.md §4 — a populated field is not a measured one).
_scope_2026_09_01: ⭐ ONE GOAL, DELIBERATELY. trimcrae: 'For now, the loop should just track the goal of the ASO paper.' The schema admits more; adding one is a decision, not a formality, because a goals file that accumulates aspirations is a wish list and this repository already has a ledger for work.

goals.title: PUB-ASO is submission-ready for its v2 preprint post
goals.set_by: trimcrae, 2026-08-30, verbatim: "Pursue the goal of getting ASO v2 submission ready regardless of weekly budget."
goals._set_by_note: Recorded verbatim rather than paraphrased. The same sentence is the authority for the budget exception in autonomy-state.json `budget_hold.authorised_exceptions`; this row does not restate that grant, it points at it — the grant is about SPEND and this row is about the OBJECTIVE, and they went stale together once already by being one sentence in one place.

done_condition.requires: every clause passes on the commit being posted
done_condition._reads: n_passed == n_clauses. ⛔ The clause COUNT is read from the tool's output, never typed here — CLAUDE.md rule 1, and this file has already watched a hard-coded 'six' go stale in a sibling record when a seventh clause landed.

goals._what_done_does_not_mean: ⛔ IT DOES NOT MEAN POSTED. `publish_bar` at full marks says the paper MAY be posted; PUB-ASO is excluded by name from the standing aiXiv grant and its Qeios v2 post is trimcrae's own act (publication-authority.json `scope.excluded_papers`). This goal completes when the paper is READY and he is told; the posting is his and is not part of the condition.
goals._blocks_on_a_human_note: ⚠ Set false ON EVIDENCE, and it was wrong for several hours on 2026-09-01. The Zenodo publish that clause 1 depends on was believed to be trimcrae's act and was escalated to him; publication-authority.json `zenodo_archive_publication` has granted it to the loop since 2026-08-30, with the per-publication approval retired the same day. See AUT-PD-196. Nothing between here and READY needs a human.
authorises: Spend against the weekly budget hold for work on this goal only — autonomy-state.json `budget_hold.authorised_exceptions`, the 2026-08-30 grant.
The hardening rounds needed to reach full marks, and the gates those require.

readings._note: All three bind to the commit being posted, and the manuscript moved after round 28's repairs, so all three are open against the current HEAD. ⭐ THE STRUCTURAL FINDING THIS READING EXISTS TO CARRY: the deposit flow required a manuscript edit (a new version DOI) AFTER the round that closes the clauses, so a clean round could not converge. Checklist §3-vi now orders it reserve → repoint → PIN → round + PREFLIGHT_FULL → refresh → publish, which is the first ordering under which this goal can reach full marks.

readings.by: interactive session, on trimcrae's report that v2 is live
readings._note:
⭐ FULL MARKS AT THE REVIEWED PIN, AND THE EVENT THIS READING EXISTS TO CARRY IS THAT THE POST HAS HAPPENED. `goal_progress.py` computes 8/8 at `3d5c709b69bc32a00a7776bf47303771d17d87f5` (round 34, 0 blockers, 7 P1s reported and not gating). The same tool reads 7/8 at HEAD 31540d962ad1, open on `preflight_full_green` alone — no PREFLIGHT_FULL receipt exists for that commit — and the manuscript is byte-identical between the two, so that is the clause-binds-to-a-commit effect the 2026-09-01 reading already named, not movement in the paper.
⛔ AND THE GOAL'S SUBJECT IS NOW BEHIND IT: Qeios v2 went live 2026-09-04T10:29:02Z as `VL3LJR.2`, posted by trimcrae, verified at primary source — `systems/graph/publications.json` → `PUB-ASO.posted` owns the identifiers. This goal says 'submission-ready for its v2 preprint post', and that post is done, so what the loop should now be working toward for this paper is an open question rather than a derivation. ⛔ `state` is deliberately LEFT `open`: closing it would drop the only goal this file tracks (`_scope_2026_09_01`: 'For now, the loop should just track the goal of the ASO paper'), and choosing its successor is trimcrae's, not a cycle's.
